## Projects and funding {#project-archive}

The laboratory’s projects, grants and contract research, with their project periods.

<details class="project-program" open>
<summary>Russian Science Foundation <span>04</span></summary>

- RSF No. 24-29-00172. Improving non-orthogonal multiple access communication systems using polar codes. 2024–2025. [RSF project record](https://rscf.ru/project/24-29-00172/).
- RSF No. 22-79-10148. Advanced multiple access methods for future 6G wireless communication systems. 2022-2025. [RSF project record](https://rscf.ru/project/22-79-10148/).
- RSF No. 21-79-00160. Communication resource allocation in telecommunication systems with non-orthogonal multiple access. 2021-2023.
- RSF No. 19-79-00087. Using non-orthogonal multiple access methods for wireless communication systems. 2019-2021.

</details>

<details id="start-1" class="project-program" open>
<summary>Start <span>01</span></summary>

- Development of a broadband reconfigurable metasurface to improve wireless communications in the 4.4–5.0 GHz band. 2026–2027.

</details>

<details class="project-program" open>
<summary>Priority 2030 <span>10</span></summary>

- Adaptation of polar codes to heterogeneous transmission channels (2026). The team registered software for optimizing the mapping of coded bits to physical resources.
- Rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA, 2024–2026). The team built a simulation model with polar coding, developed adaptive precoding and power allocation algorithms, and studied operation under overload.
- Development of a STAR-RIS intelligent reflecting surface for future wireless communication systems. 2025.
- Common-stream precoding algorithms for RSMA systems (2024–2025). Artyom Shinkevich led the study.
- Adaptation of polar codes to the channel state. 2023.
- Simulation of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes for 5G NR. In 2021, an individual TUSUR grant supported a review of the 3GPP specifications, including the structure of the parity-check matrix and the characteristics of the encoder. In 2022, the laboratory developed a simulation model of a communication system with LDPC coding and evaluated its error performance.
- Research on the efficiency of polar codes for a broad class of channel models. 2022.
- Experimental study of PD-NOMA non-orthogonal multiple access for 6G networks. 2022. In a separate project on improving spectral efficiency, the team modeled PD-NOMA and SCMA for the Internet of Things in 2022. In 2023, it developed a PD-NOMA model for robotic devices and an algorithm for selecting SCMA codebook parameters.
- Development of an experimental prototype of a multichannel communication system with non-orthogonal multiple access. 2021.
- Concept and architecture of a software suite for generating and analyzing 5G NR signals (2021). Yakov Kryukov led the project.

</details>

<details class="project-program" open>
<summary>TUSUR Advanced Engineering School <span>03</span></summary>

- Development of methods and algorithms for digital distortion compensation in wireless communication systems. 2024-2026.
- Development of a communication channel model with a reconfigurable intelligent surface. 2023-2025.
- Development of channel coding algorithms for 5G NR communication systems. 2023-2025.

</details>

<details class="project-program" open>
<summary>UMNIK <span>04</span></summary>

- Development of an intelligent software system for determining digital signal parameters using machine learning. 2026–2027.
- Development of the ReCK-RIS hardware and software system for controlling a reconfigurable metasurface. 2026–2027.
- Development of a reconfigurable intelligent surface. 2024-2025.
- Software for adaptive LDPC and polar codecs (2022–2024). Georgy Shalin led the project.

</details>

<details class="project-program" open>
<summary>Industry Contracts <span>02</span></summary>

- Collaboration with Skoltech in 2019–2021. In 2019, the team developed algorithms for generating and processing ultra-narrowband Open UNB signals. In 2020–2021, it estimated how many users a 5G base station could serve with limited computing resources and calculated channel throughput in an open-architecture 5G network. The team also used machine learning to model radio channels for ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) and developed a random access model to estimate collisions when many devices connect.
- Collaboration with Micran in 2024 on software development and signal processing algorithms for radio-relay modems.

</details>

<details class="project-program" open>
<summary>Individual Grants <span>02</span></summary>

- Presidential Grant 2021. Signal generation and processing methods in multi-antenna communication systems with sparse-code multiple access, No. 075-15-2021-071. 2021-2022.
- Presidential Grant 2019. Adaptive channel-state-dependent signal structures for sparse-code multiple access communication systems, No. 075-15-2019-374. 2019-2020.

</details>
